'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[2024 Syrian opposition offensives]]
***[[2024 Homs offensive]]
****After capturing the town of [[Talbiseh]] and the city of [[Al-Rastan]], rebel forces capture several more towns and villages in the northern countryside of [[Homs Governorate]], [[Syria]], reaching the town of [[Al-Dar al-Kabirah]] and approaching the outskirts of [[Homs]]. [https://www.syriahr.com/en/350716/ (SOHR)] [https://www.aa.com.tr/ar/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%B1%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A9/%D8%B3%D9%88%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A7-%D9%81%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%B9%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%B6%D8%A9-%D8%AA%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%B5%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D9%88%D8%BA%D9%84-%D8%A8%D9%85%D8%AF%D9%8A%D9%86%D8%A9-%D8%AD%D9%85%D8%B5/3416211 (Anadolu Agency)]
****[[Russian Air Force|Russian]] and [[Syrian Air Force|Syrian]] warplanes bombard rebel-held areas in Homs Governorate, killing at least 20 people. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cwy8xzxe0w7t (BBC News)]
**[[Southern Syria offensive (2024)|Southern Syria offensive]]
***[[Syrian Army]] soldiers from the [[8th Armoured Division (Syria)|8th Armoured Division]] in [[Daraa]] defect to the [[Syrian opposition]] as rebels launch attacks on pro-[[government of Syria|government]] checkpoints across [[Daraa Governorate]], taking control of several towns, including [[Inkhil]], [[Ghabaghib]], and [[Al-Jiza, Syria|al-Jiza]], as well as the city of [[Jasim]]. Rebels later claim near total control of the governorate. [https://www.yenisafak.com/en/news/clashes-intensify-in-syrias-southern-province-of-daraa-3695387 (Yeni Safak)]
***Rebels take full control of the city of Daraa after agreeing to allow [[Ba'ath Party (Syrian-dominated faction)|Ba'ath Party]] officials to leave the city with safe passage to [[Damascus]], and also take full control of the mainly [[Druze]] city of [[Suwayda]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/syrian-rebels-take-over-southern-city-of-daraa-in-deal-with-army-rebel-sources/ (''The Times of Israel'')] [https://www.newarab.com/news/syrian-regime-collapses-daraa-and-east-dozens-killed-gaza (The New Arab)] [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/clashes-intensify-in-syrias-southern-province-of-daraa/3416138 (Anadolu Agency)] [https://www.newsweek.com/syria-civil-war-live-updates-syrian-state-media-denies-damascus-under-attack-rebels-advance-1996713 (''Newsweek'')]
***[[Jordan]] closes [[Jordan–Syria border|its border]] with Syria after rebel forces seize the main [[Nasib Border Crossing]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/jordan-closes-border-crossing-into-syria-ministry-says-2024-12-06/ (Reuters)]
**[[Deir ez-Zor offensive (2024)|Deir ez-Zor offensive]]
***The [[Kurds in Syria|Kurdish]]-led [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] take control of [[Deir ez-Zor]] and [[Deir ez-Zor Airport|its airport]] following the withdrawal of pro-government forces. [https://english.enabbaladi.net/archives/2024/12/syrian-regime-withdraws-forces-from-deir-ezzor/ (Enab Baladi)] [https://www.syriahr.com/en/350727/ (SOHR)]
***[[Iraq]]i militias withdraw from the Syrian side of the [[Al-Qa'im border crossing]] on [[Iraq–Syria border|the border]] with Iraq. [https://shafaq.com/en/Iraq/Iraqi-factions-withdraw-from-Syria-toward-Al-Qaim-as-SDF-seizes-Al-Bukamal-crossing (Shafaq)]
**[[Russia–Syria relations]]
***[[Russia]] tells its citizens to leave Syria on commercial flights while they still can amid rebel advances in the country. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/world/2024/12/06/russia-tells-its-nationals-to-leave-syria (Al Arabiya)]
**[[Turkish involvement in the Syrian civil war]]
***[[Turkey]] [[asset freezing|freezes the assets]] of deceased former commander of Tahrir al-Sham [[Abu Maria al-Qahtani]], who was killed in April, to comply with the [[United Nations Security Council]]'s policies. [https://www.turkishminute.com/2024/12/06/turkey-froze-assets-of-late-islamic-militant-leader-link-hts/ (''Turkish Minute'')]
**[[Tahrir al-Sham]] leader [[Abu Mohammad al-Julani]] says that his forces will not end their military campaign until [[President of Syria|Syrian president]] [[Bashar al-Assad]] is removed from power. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20241206-syria-rebel-leader-says-goal-is-to-overthrow-assad (France 24)]
**[[Egypt]] and Jordan both urge Bashar al-Assad and [[Al-Assad family|his family]] to leave Syria, saying that Assad can no longer stop the rebel offensive. [https://www.wsj.com/world/middle-east/syrian-rebels-advance-on-third-major-city-in-growing-threat-to-assad-bd21f39f (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
**The [[India]]n [[Ministry of External Affairs (India)|Ministry of External Affairs]] advises its citizens to leave Syria and avoid all travel to the country indefinitely. [https://www.wionews.com/world/indians-advised-to-leave-syria-at-the-earliest-as-bashar-al-assad-loses-control-of-another-city-782177 (WION)]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Kamal Adwan Hospital sieges]]
***[[Israel]]i drone strikes on the northern and western sides of the Kamal Adwan Hospital in [[Beit Lahia]] in the [[Gaza Strip]] kill at least 29 [[Palestinians]]. Israeli forces subsequently raid the hospital, killing four doctors. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/12/6/live-israel-kills-dozens-in-gaza-continues-to-target-southern-lebanon (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.cnn.com/2024/12/06/middleeast/kamal-adwan-gaza-israel-hospital-raid-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Southern front of the Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] missile strike kills ten [[civilian]]s in [[Zaporizhzhia]], [[Ukraine]], and injures four others, including two children. Separately, a missile attack on an administrative building in [[Kryvyi Rih]], Ukraine, kills two people and injures 16 others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-missile-kills-two-wounds-13-ukraines-kryvyi-rih-2024-12-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[EU–Mercosur Association Agreement]]
**The [[European Union]] and [[Mercosur]] trade bloc finalize a free trade deal in [[Montevideo]], [[Uruguay]], after 25 years of negotiations. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20241206-%F0%9F%94%B4-european-union-and-mercosur-trade-bloc-finalise-contentious-free-trade-agreement (France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024–25 European windstorm season]]
**Millions of people receive [[UK Emergency Alert System|emergency alerts]] in the [[United Kingdom]] as [[Storm Darragh]] prepares to make landfall over the [[British Isles]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c2dxlwz219ko (BBC News)]
*Twenty-six people are killed and 28 more injured after a collision between two [[minibus]]es in Brokoua, [[Ivory Coast]]. [https://apnews.com/article/ivory-coast-road-accident-bf1242dae98700c462d9cbb26987cb21 (AP)]
*[[New Zealand Police]] [[Presumption of death|presume]] that two [[Americans]] and a [[Canadian]] are dead after evidence suggests they fell while attempting to [[Mountaineering|summit]] [[Aoraki / Mount Cook|Mount Cook (Aoraki)]], suspending search operations. [https://edition.cnn.com/2024/12/06/us/us-canada-climbers-new-zealand-hnk-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Belarus–Russia relations]], [[Nuclear risk during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] and [[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] sign an agreement in [[Minsk]], [[Belarus]], offering security guarantees to Belarus including [[Nuclear safety and security|nuclear security]] and the possible use of [[Russia and weapons of mass destruction|Russian nuclear weapons]] in order to repel aggressions. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-belarus-security-agreement-nuclear-doctrine-c07ef5d341f93be6934ac14a77b58f8b (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Antisemitism in Australia]]
**Two people are injured in an [[Arson|arson attack]] on a [[synagogue]] in [[Melbourne]], [[Australia]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/australia-police-suspect-arson-attack-at-synagogue/a-70979260 (DW)] [https://www.australianjewishnews.com/adass-shul-blaze-suspicious/ (''The Australian Jewish News'')]
*[[Restrictions on TikTok in the United States]]
**A [[United States court of appeals]] upholds the [[Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act]], which requires [[China]]-based company [[ByteDance]] to sell [[TikTok]] by January 19 or face an effective ban on operations in the [[United States]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2024/12/06/tiktok-divestment-law-upheld-by-federal-appeals-court.html (CNBC)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2024 Aruban general election]]
**[[Aruba]]ns vote to elect the 21 members of the [[Parliament of Aruba|Parliament]]. The [[Aruban People's Party]] wins nine seats and the [[People's Electoral Movement (Aruba)|People's Electoral Movement]] wins eight seats, neither parties achieving a [[majority]]. [https://arubapapers.com/aruba-prepares-for-election-day-tomorrow-why-youre-seeing-colored-flags-everywhere/ (''Aruba Papers'')]
*[[2024 Mauritian presidential election]]
**An [[uncontested election]] is held for the [[President of Mauritius]], with former minister of education and [[Labour Party (Mauritius)|Labour Party]] representative [[Dharam Gokhool]] [[walkover|winning without contest]]. [[Robert Hungley]] is elected [[Vice-President of Mauritius|Vice-President]]. [https://english.news.cn/20241207/099e2e3939774046a018b86ed5a253ca/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[2024 Romanian presidential election]]
**The [[Constitutional Court of Romania]] annuls the first round results of the presidential election vote two days before the second round of the election. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2024/12/06/romania-election-president-georgescu-court/d43bd9e2-b3d4-11ef-9d23-e5faa22ad216_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
